statement: An estimated 70 million or more people worldwide live with vitiligo (0.5%–2.0% global prevalence).
clinicalBasis: Extrapolated from worldwide epidemiological studies; ranges vary significantly by country (e.g. higher reported incidence in parts of India, lower in Nordic countries).
boardActionRequired: Review whether to present a single 70M figure or a dynamic range (0.5% to 2.0% of world population, ~40M–160M) based on current Global Vitiligo Foundation consensus.

statement: AAD notes an estimated 12%–38% of people with vitiligo have some degree of hearing loss due to inner ear melanocytes.
clinicalBasis: Stria vascularis in the cochlea contains melanocytes essential for endocochlear potential. While subclinical sensorineural loss is documented in studies, routine audiometric screening is not universal in standard clinical practice.
boardActionRequired: Confirm clinical phrasing so patients are advised of the association without inducing undue alarm or unwarranted urgent audiograms.

statement: Thyroid peroxidase antibodies (TPOAb) and TSH blood tests are recommended periodically for individuals with generalized vitiligo.
clinicalBasis: Autoimmune thyroid disease is the most common comorbidity (15%–25% in various cohorts).
boardActionRequired: Confirm whether the hub should specify a baseline check and annual or bi-annual interval for pediatric and adult cohorts.

statement: There is no scientific evidence that specific food combinations (e.g. fish with milk or sour foods) cause or worsen vitiligo.
clinicalBasis: Strong consensus in dermatology (IADVL, AAD, EADV); cultural dietary restrictions frequently cause nutritional deficiencies without affecting vitiligo course.
boardActionRequired: Approve explicit anti-stigma messaging to encourage balanced nutrition without guilt.

statement: Noticeable follicular repigmentation typically begins around 8 to 12 weeks of treatment; full response requires 6 to 12+ months.
clinicalBasis: Dependent on anatomical site (acral vs facial), disease duration, and compliance.
boardActionRequired: Approve standard disclaimers stating that acral (hands/feet) and mucosal areas may have limited repigmentation.
